title: Register Convention: Booking an Upgrade Credit and Revaluing It Upward
content:
The credit under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes is booked as available to spend on the day it is issued, and it is booked once against the registration it belongs to.

## Standing required

Credit is booked, and later revalued, only while the registration stands at credit issued or partially redeemed. The standing is read from the registration before the entry is made.

## Revaluation upward

On the programmes that allow it, an issued credit may be revalued upward inside the programme's revaluation window, counted from the day the credit was issued, and the increase is booked as its own entry. The revaluation window is counted in whole calendar days from the day the credit was issued, that day counting as day zero, weekends and store holidays included. The day the credit was issued is the issue date on the registration; the window is met while the handling date is not later than the issue date plus the programme's window in calendar days, and a handling date that lands exactly on the last day of the window is within it.

A credit is never revalued downward once issued: where the piece proves to be worth less than valued, the credit is withdrawn in full and the piece returned rather than quietly reduced.

Whether a programme allows revaluation, the length of its window and the number of days its credit lasts are the programme's published figures.

## Window boundary cases

Take a programme with a revaluation window of 60 calendar days and a credit issued on a given day, that day being day zero.

| Handling date | Days since issue | Within the window |
|---|---|---|
| the 59th day after issue | 59 | yes |
| the 60th day after issue | 60 | yes, on the boundary day |
| the 61st day after issue | 61 | no |

Under a programme whose window is published as 0, and which does not allow revaluation, no upward revaluation is booked at all.
